issues.description: The problem statement (UML) declares ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel as type double, but the solution implementation declares excellencyLevel as int (and uses int in the constructor and getter). This is an attribute type mismatch: students following the UML will implement a constructor and getter using double, while the provided solution (and possibly tests) use int, which may break compilation/tests or confuse students about the intended type.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the type for excellencyLevel consistent. Preferably change the solution to match the UML: declare excellencyLevel as double, update the constructor parameter to double, and change the getter to return double. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use int if an integer level was intended—ensure all artifacts (problem, template, tests, solution) use the same type.
